nodes.label: forget vs forget_all Selection Guidance
nodes.rationale: forget_all is the bulk hammer for screen teardown (cancel every stream of a type); forget is surgical, cancelling one subscription ID while sibling streams of the same type keep running. Choosing forget_all when only one stream should die silently kills the others.

nodes.label: Health Polling Best Practices (30-60s, exponential backoff)
nodes.norm_label: health polling best practices (30-60s, exponential backoff)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-interval polling with a short timeout detects slow responses as well as hard failures; exponential backoff on repeated failures prevents a monitoring client from amplifying an outage into a thundering-herd retry storm.

nodes.label: WebSocket Keep-Alive via Ping (30-60s)
nodes.rationale: Proxies and firewalls close idle WebSocket connections; a periodic ping keeps traffic flowing so the socket is not silently dropped. req_id lets each pong be matched to its ping, which also yields a latency measurement.

nodes.label: Clock Synchronisation Offset
nodes.rationale: Contract expiry (date_expiry) is expressed in server epoch seconds; a client whose local clock drifts would compute wrong expiry times, so the offset between local and server clocks must be measured and applied to time-sensitive contract operations.

nodes.label: Direct Buy via parameters (buy=1) vs Proposal ID
nodes.norm_label: direct buy via parameters (buy=1) vs proposal id
nodes.rationale: Passing buy="1" with a full parameters object skips the proposal round-trip, trading price certainty for latency; the price field caps the maximum acceptable purchase price so an adverse move between quote and execution rejects rather than fills at a worse price.

nodes.label: Relative Barrier Rule for Sub-24h Contracts
nodes.norm_label: relative barrier rule for sub-24h contracts
nodes.rationale: Contracts shorter than 24 hours require a relative barrier (+/- offset from entry spot) because the absolute price level is unknowable at request time; Synthetic Indices are exempt since their spot series is generated and both relative and absolute barriers are meaningful. For digit contracts the barrier field doubles as the last-digit prediction.

nodes.label: Non-Streamed Proposal Symbols (R_10..R_100, RDBULL, RDBEAR)
nodes.rationale: Tick trades without a user-defined barrier, digit trades, and sub-24h at-the-money contracts on R_10/R_25/R_50/R_75/R_100/RDBULL/RDBEAR are not streamed because their price is constant — a subscription would emit no new information, so the API refuses to open one.

nodes.label: Sell at Market (price = 0)
nodes.rationale: price acts as a minimum acceptable sale price, protecting against slippage; passing 0 explicitly waives that protection and accepts whatever the market offers, which is the right choice when exiting a position matters more than the exit price.

nodes.label: Common Patterns (subscription cleanup, req_id matching, reconnect)
nodes.norm_label: common patterns (subscription cleanup, req_id matching, reconnect)
nodes.rationale: Because the WebSocket multiplexes many concurrent request/response pairs over one socket, a unique req_id per request is the only reliable way to correlate a response with its caller. Subscription IDs must be stored so streams can be cleaned up before disconnect, and after a reconnect the client must re-authenticate and re-subscribe since server-side stream state does not survive the socket.

nodes.label: Pipeline Genético com Drift Test
nodes.rationale: Particionamento triplo de dados (A: Descoberta, B: Validação FDR, C: Reserva Monte Carlo) com driftTest para descartar estratégias sobreajustadas.

nodes.label: Modelagem Estatística Pura (Lanczos, Chi2, Gamma, Binomial)
nodes.norm_label: modelagem estatistica pura (lanczos, chi2, gamma, binomial)
nodes.rationale: Implementação em TypeScript puro sem dependências externas de lgamma via Lanczos, gammaP, chiP, binomP e erfc de Abramowitz & Stegun.

nodes.label: Motor 2.0 e Classificação das 17 Lógicas
nodes.rationale: Divisão em 10 lógicas FDR (Fmin, Markov, Paridade, Gaps, etc.), 6 lógicas Wide em bloco e 1 de Exaustão Extrema com pontuação composta ponderada por genoma.

nodes.label: Esteira Genética e Validação Tripla
nodes.rationale: Garante estratégias robustas contra overfitting particionando dados em A (descoberta), B (validação FDR) e C (reserva com 50 permutações de Monte Carlo).

nodes.label: Simulação de Ruína de Monte Carlo
nodes.norm_label: simulacao de ruina de monte carlo
nodes.rationale: Geração de trajetórias sintéticas com 1000 iterações para projetar probabilidade de drawdown >= 25%, 50% e ruína total.

nodes.label: Teste de Quebra de Regime (Drift Test)
nodes.norm_label: teste de quebra de regime (drift test)
nodes.rationale: Compara distribuições da 1ª e 2ª metade da amostra via distância estatística para detectar alterações estruturais no gerador da corretora.

nodes.label: Manual Técnico de Arquitetura Bear Bot Differ
nodes.norm_label: manual tecnico de arquitetura bear bot differ

nodes.label: Regras de Ouro de Gestão de Risco Differ
nodes.norm_label: regras de ouro de gestao de risco differ
nodes.rationale: Respeito incondicional ao Stop Loss, uso obrigatório de Loss Virtual em conta real, metas diárias de 1-3% e preferência por Martingale Parcial.

nodes.label: Controle FDR de Benjamini-Hochberg (q=0.10)
nodes.rationale: Mitiga proliferação de falsos positivos na avaliação simultânea das 10 lógicas em competição ativa ordenando p-valores sob critério estocástico.

nodes.label: Critério de Kelly Fracionário (Half & Quarter Kelly)
nodes.norm_label: criterio de kelly fracionario (half & quarter kelly)
nodes.rationale: Determinação matemática da fração ideal de alocação de banca ajustada para o payout assimétrico do Differ, mitigando volatilidade extrema.

nodes.label: Pontuação Composta de Dígitos (scoreAll)
nodes.rationale: S(d) = w_gap*NormGap + w_freq*NormFreq + w_markov*NormMarkov + w_parity*NormParity selecionando o dígito com maior score como barreira Differ.

nodes.label: Cooldown Ticks
nodes.rationale: Ticks are ignored for a configured count after each trade so the bot does not immediately re-enter on the same still-satisfied condition.

nodes.label: SIMULADO/REAL Mode Switching
nodes.rationale: Consecutive simulated wins promote the bot to REAL and any real streak (win or loss) demotes it back to SIMULADO, so real capital is only exposed after the strategy proves itself on paper.

nodes.label: startExecution (isExecutionActive)
nodes.rationale: Flipping isExecutionActive is the exact moment active execution monitoring begins; rule evaluation runs on every tick only from that point.

nodes.label: LegacyBridge Integration Layer
nodes.rationale: Legacy scripts are loaded as dynamic <script> tags and communicate through window globals and CustomEvents, with shims (CreditsManager, UserLevels, selectedSymbol, logConfig) standing in for removed legacy subsystems.

nodes.label: URL Ingest (graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects YouTube/video, Twitter/X oEmbed, arXiv, PDF, image and generic webpage URLs, saving each into ./raw for the next --update to merge.

nodes.label: Watch Mode
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; doc/image changes only raise a needs_update flag since they require paid semantic re-extraction. The 3s debounce keeps a wave of parallel agent writes from triggering one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path over stdio so other agents can query the graph live. Claude Desktop must be given the absolute interpreter path since it cannot run $(...) and system python3 cannot import graphify under uv tool install.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Only runs above 5,000 words — for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Hyperedges
nodes.rationale: Capped at 3 per chunk and used only when a 3+ node group relationship adds information beyond the pairwise edges.

nodes.label: Semantic Similarity Edges
nodes.rationale: Links concepts that solve the same problem with no structural link (no import, call or citation) — reserved for genuinely non-obvious cross-cutting similarity.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo Graph Merge
nodes.rationale: Running the skill per subfolder would clobber the shared graphify-out/ dir, so the CLI is used per path (which nests graphify-out inside each) and merge-graphs combines them; each merged node carries a repo attribute for filtering.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of running a background process, works with any editor, and appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: BFS/DFS Traversal Modes
nodes.rationale: BFS answers 'what is X connected to' with nearest neighbors first; DFS (depth-limited to 6) traces 'how does X reach Y' without walking the whole graph.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query matcher is case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch returns 0 hits; expanding against the graph's own vocab file (max 12 real tokens, never invented) is the fix, and the selection is printed so it is auditable.

nodes.label: save-result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Persisting the Q&A (with the expanded-token trace inside the answer) means the next --update extracts the expansion history as a graph node, closing the loop so future queries improve.

nodes.label: Work Memory and LESSONS.md
nodes.rationale: Outcomes tagged useful / dead_end / corrected accumulate into preferred sources, known dead ends and prior corrections; `reflect --if-stale` is deterministic and free, so refreshing lessons at session start costs almost nothing.

nodes.label: Whisper Video/Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: The host agent writes the Whisper initial prompt itself from god-node labels — it is already a language model, so no separate API call is needed; transcripts are then treated as ordinary doc files.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction survives (#801); prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files because changed files are reconciled by replace-on-re-extract (#1344), and root= must be passed or nothing is pruned and stale nodes accumulate (#1361).

nodes.label: --cluster-only Mode
nodes.rationale: Self-contained: re-running Steps 5-9 after it would hit FileNotFoundError because the prior build's cleanup already deleted the intermediate files (#1392).

nodes.label: Incremental --update Flow
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new or changed files to save tokens and time; code-only changes skip semantic extraction entirely because AST is deterministic and needs no LLM.

nodes.label: AST Structural Extraction (Part A)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — code needs no LLM and no API key at all, so a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely.

nodes.label: Community Detection and Labeling
nodes.rationale: Clusters get 2-5 word human labels; questions are regenerated after labeling because labels change question phrasing, and graph.json is re-exported so nodes carry community_name (#2490).

nodes.label: Corpus Detection Step
nodes.rationale: Gates on 2M words / 500 files and reports skipped_sensitive so a wrongly-flagged source is visible rather than silently dropped (#2106).

nodes.label: Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only gate that never aborts — it surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops, the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches.

nodes.label: Graphify Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Nine ordered steps (detect, transcribe, extract, build/cluster, health check, label, export, cleanup) so any corpus of code, docs, papers, images or video becomes one navigable graph with an honest audit trail.

nodes.label: Python Interpreter Resolution
nodes.rationale: uv tool / pipx / venv installs mean the system python3 often cannot import graphify, so the resolved interpreter path is persisted to .graphify_python for every subsequent step.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are stamped with the SPEC_PATH prompt that produced them, so a prompt upgrade re-extracts instead of replaying stale results (#1939).

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction (Part B)
nodes.rationale: Only docs, papers and images need an LLM; parallel general-purpose subagents are mandatory because reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower, and Explore subagents are read-only and silently drop chunk files.

nodes.label: Graphify Always-On Rule
nodes.rationale: Codebase/architecture questions should hit the pre-built graph first because a scoped subgraph from query/path/explain is far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, saving context tokens.

nodes.label: Call Edge Direction and Language Rule
nodes.norm_label: call edge direction and language rule
nodes.rationale: Source must always be the caller and calls edges must stay within one language — cross-language call edges are phantom artifacts.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: A discrete five-value set (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replaces a continuous range because production showed models collapsing the range to a binary — >50% at 0.5 and >40% at 0.85+.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative path segments must all be kept so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the id matches what the AST extractor generates; chunk suffixes are banned so ids are deterministic regardless of which chunk processes an entity.

nodes.label: Rationale-as-Attribute Rule
nodes.rationale: WHY-decisions are stored as a rationale attribute on the relevant concept node rather than as separate rationale/fragment nodes, so only real named entities become nodes.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path character-for-character keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: Fast Path for Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely — rebuilding costs tokens and time for an answer the graph already contains.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS), never skip the corpus warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, never render >5000 nodes without warning — the graph's value is that its uncertainty is auditable.

nodes.label: Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped; a doc whose chunk failed stays unstamped so the next --update re-queues it instead of losing its content forever (#2015, #1948, #1908).

nodes.label: No-API-Key Policy
nodes.rationale: Graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY; only GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY are optional. Blocking on a key is a misread of the skill — the host agent itself is the fallback LLM.

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json returns False rather than writing a graph smaller than the existing one (#479); the report and analysis sidecar are only written when the graph was actually written, so they never describe a graph graph.json doesn't contain (#1392).

nodes.label: Deriv REST Error Response Format (errors[] + meta)
nodes.norm_label: deriv rest error response format (errors[] + meta)

nodes.label: Market Data Workflow (public endpoint, no auth)
nodes.norm_label: market data workflow (public endpoint, no auth)

nodes.label: Demo vs Real Account Types
nodes.rationale: Demo accounts hold virtual funds so strategies can be validated without capital risk; real accounts require verification and funding. The 200-vs-201 status split exists so an idempotent create call can distinguish an already-existing account (single object) from a freshly provisioned one (array).

nodes.label: Demo-Only Balance Reset Constraint ($10,000 default)
nodes.rationale: Only demo accounts may be reset because virtual funds carry no financial meaning; allowing a real-account reset would amount to minting money. Attempting it returns 400 ValidationError rather than silently ignoring the request.

nodes.label: Options Typical Workflow (account then OTP then WebSocket)
nodes.norm_label: options typical workflow (account then otp then websocket)
nodes.rationale: Account setup is done over REST because it is a one-off provisioning step, while trading needs a persistent low-latency channel; the OTP endpoint bridges the two by embedding a short-lived credential in the WebSocket URL so the socket itself needs no auth headers.

nodes.label: OTP Lifetime (short-lived, use immediately)
nodes.rationale: The OTP travels as a URL query parameter, which is a comparatively leaky channel (logs, proxies, referrers); making it single-shot and short-lived bounds the damage window. Expired tokens are recovered by re-calling the OTP endpoint rather than by refreshing in place.

nodes.label: Workflow B: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE
nodes.norm_label: workflow b: oauth 2.0 authorization code with pkce
nodes.rationale: OAuth is chosen for browser apps that can handle redirects: it issues short-lived (typically 3600s) access tokens so the user never shares a password and long-term credential exposure is minimised. The state parameter must be validated to block CSRF, and code_challenge/code_verifier (S256) binds the authorization code to the originating client. Every redirect URL including subdirectories must be whitelisted exactly.

nodes.label: Workflow A: PAT-Based Authentication
nodes.rationale: PAT apps are chosen when browser redirects are impractical (desktop tools, CLI apps, native clients): the user pastes a long-lived Personal Access Token instead of running a redirect dance. The trade-off is a long-lived credential that must be stored securely and can only be revoked manually.

nodes.label: Workflows Troubleshooting (401/403, legacy App ID, expired token)
nodes.norm_label: workflows troubleshooting (401/403, legacy app id, expired token)
nodes.rationale: Legacy App IDs deliberately do not work with the new APIs, so an app registered before the migration must be re-registered on developers.deriv.com. Token type must match app type — a PAT used against an OAuth-type app (or vice versa) yields 401 even when the token itself is valid; 403 instead means the token is valid but lacks the trade or account_manage scope.

nodes.label: Legacy Rules Cache and History API
nodes.norm_label: legacy rules cache and history api

nodes.label: Legacy Script Load Order
nodes.rationale: The ~70 legacy scripts have no module system, so they are injected as <script> tags in strict dependency order (utils, indicators, management, validators, AI, execution); injection is idempotent to survive re-mounts.

nodes.label: Window Global Shims
nodes.rationale: CreditsManager and UserLevels are stubbed to always grant credits and VIP so the legacy paywall logic no longer gates anything.

nodes.label: Group Activation Logic
nodes.rationale: Each rule group can be switched on or off by the previous result crossed with the mode (win/loss x real/simulated), letting a strategy rotate entry conditions after each outcome.

nodes.label: Gemini Model Selection by Group Count
nodes.norm_label: gemini model selection by group count
nodes.rationale: Model size scales with strategy complexity — 1 group uses 2.5 Flash (128k), 2 groups 2.5 Pro (1M), 3+ groups 3.0 Pro — so simple strategies do not pay for a large-context model.

nodes.label: Rule Compatibility Validator
nodes.rationale: Must always run after translation and before execution, because an AI-generated rule set can reference indicators incompatible with the selected contract type.

nodes.label: Strategy Cache (7-day TTL)
nodes.rationale: Keys are hashed under strategy_cache_global with a 7-day TTL, and per-user history lives in rules_history_<loginId>.

nodes.label: translateStrategy Pipeline
nodes.rationale: preprocess -> validate -> four-tier lookup (JSON cache, rule code, historical rules, translation cache) -> Gemini fallback, so a paid AI call only happens when no cheaper source can answer.

nodes.label: toggleBot Start Handler
nodes.rationale: Validates symbol and translated rules, loads legacy scripts, pushes React UI config into the legacy trade manager, then arms monitoring — the single entry point from the INICIAR button.

nodes.label: AdvancedRulesEngine (Modo Avancado)
nodes.rationale: Accepts complex natural-language strategies, has the AI emit json-rules-engine JSON, keeps a rolling 200-tick buffer, computes facts per tick and fires window.tradeManager.executeTrade() on a match.

nodes.label: Strategy Translation Flow
nodes.rationale: Resolves cheapest-first — JSON cache, then rule code, then history, then translation cache — with the paid Gemini AI call only as a last-resort fallback.

nodes.label: CustomEvent Interceptors
nodes.rationale: Legacy CustomEvents (trade-result, mode-change, stop-triggered, pause-start/end) are translated into Observer callbacks so React never listens to the legacy DOM directly.

nodes.label: TypeScript Language Server Backend
nodes.rationale: TypeScript is the single configured language server for bot-trader; for JavaScript files Serena also uses the typescript server.

nodes.label: window.tradeManager (trade-manager.js)
nodes.rationale: The real contract purchase against the Deriv WebSocket still lives in legacy JS — React only signals it, which is why trade execution is listed as not yet migrated.

nodes.label: setupTradeMessageInterceptor
nodes.rationale: Captures the WIN/LOSS outcome from the legacy layer and hands it back to React so the UI can update without React owning the trade lifecycle.

nodes.label: Dual-Layer Auth and Route Protection
nodes.rationale: Server-side middleware uses the HttpOnly auth_token cookie with jose (Edge Runtime) while the client layout redirects on getUser() failure; API routes use jsonwebtoken because they run on Node.js. Logout must clear both localStorage and the cookie.

nodes.label: bot-strategy Module (Discontinued)
nodes.rationale: Discontinued — all AI integration must now go directly through the /api/gemini endpoint instead of this module.

nodes.label: TradePlatform Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 + React 19 platform mid-migration from a legacy Vanilla JS system in public/legacy/js to a modern TypeScript/React stack.

nodes.label: Not-Yet-Migrated Surface
nodes.rationale: Trade execution, headless monitoring, the results dashboard, the automatic stop/limit system and Telegram integration still live in the legacy layer.

nodes.label: webpack TensorFlow.js Configuration
nodes.rationale: Turbopack is explicitly disabled because TensorFlow.js needs webpack-specific WASM COOP/COEP headers, fs/path/crypto fallbacks and server-side externals for utf-8-validate and bufferutil.

nodes.label: Bot Strategy Migration 2025
nodes.rationale: bot-ia moved from Vanilla JS to Next.js/React + TypeScript with credits removed for unrestricted access and a separate login dropped in favour of the app's global deriv_accounts/activeToken.

nodes.label: extractLastDigit e Pip Size por símbolo
nodes.norm_label: extractlastdigit e pip size por simbolo

nodes.label: Automatic Reconnection and Request Queue
nodes.rationale: DerivService already manages reconnection, the pending-request queue and a 25s ping, so manual retry or ping logic would duplicate it.

nodes.label: extractLastDigit
nodes.rationale: Must never be reimplemented manually — the per-symbol decimal precision table lives inside DerivService, so a hand-rolled extraction silently reads the wrong digit.

nodes.label: Tick/Balance Subscription Management
nodes.rationale: The returned subscription_id must be stored so the stream can be cancelled with { forget: id }.

nodes.label: DerivService Test Mock
nodes.rationale: WebSocket is unavailable under jsdom, so DerivService is mocked wholesale rather than connected.

nodes.label: DerivService WebSocket Singleton
nodes.rationale: Two channels: a public market gateway for ticks/ticks_history with no auth, and a trading OTP channel for buy/proposal/balance. The legacy ws.derivws.com/websockets/v3 endpoint must not be used for tick streams because it returns InvalidSymbol on synthetics.

nodes.label: Digit Precision by Symbol
nodes.rationale: Each synthetic symbol quotes a different number of decimals, so the last digit can only be read correctly with a per-symbol precision table.

nodes.label: Gap Bonus
nodes.rationale: A digit absent for 10+ ticks gets a probability boost.

nodes.label: Saturation Penalty
nodes.rationale: Above 15% frequency a digit's probability is cut proportionally to the excess, on the assumption that an over-represented digit is due to mean-revert.

nodes.label: Weighted Period Scoring
nodes.rationale: score = sum(occurrences x period weight) normalized by the weighted sample total, so the last 10 ticks dominate the estimate while the 100-tick window still anchors it.

nodes.label: Test Priority Matrix
nodes.rationale: The probability algorithm, the Gale/Soros stake math and extractLastDigit are highest priority because they carry the trading domain's money-losing edge cases; LegacyBridge is lowest because DOM injection is hard to test.

nodes.label: Singleton Reset Between Tests
nodes.rationale: MonitoringService._instance is nulled in beforeEach because a shared singleton would leak tick history between test cases.

nodes.label: localStorage Config Persistence
nodes.rationale: Configs auto-save on change under fixed keys (trade_config_trade/management/controller/full); breaking the schema requires a migration because saved user setups would otherwise be silently misread.

nodes.label: 5-Period Weighted Probability Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Recent ticks are weighted far more heavily (1-10 at 5.0 down to 1-100 at 0.5), then corrected by a saturation penalty above 15% frequency, a dynamic bias for repetitions and a gap bonus for absences of 10+ ticks.

nodes.label: BotTrader Copy Trader
nodes.rationale: Server-side chain CopyTradingManager -> CopyTradingService (per user) -> WsListener (demo WS) + TradeExecutor (real WS).

nodes.label: Martingale Stake Formula
nodes.rationale: stake(level) = initialValue x (1 + stakeMultiple)^level; a win resets the level and maxMartingale caps it with either reset or stop.

nodes.label: onTrade Guard
nodes.rationale: Prevents two simultaneous real trades — the equivalent of bool_89 in the original ZeekBot.

nodes.label: Quantity Loss Mode
nodes.rationale: Waits for N consecutive demo losses before entering the real account, and once isInRealMode is true it stays real until a win — capital is only risked after the demo stream has demonstrated a losing run.

nodes.label: ZeeK Heartbeat Telemetry
nodes.rationale: Every ~60s the app posts account identity, balance, currency, profit, wins/losses and a hash of the Deriv token to the operator's server, which acknowledges storing each one — effectively real-time surveillance of every user's account.

nodes.label: ZeeK Martingale/Soros Strategy Constants
nodes.rationale: Reconstructed only from Nuitka constant names (initial_stake, multiplier_mode, soros_factor, stop_mode, mini_meta_*, hunter/wave/focus/timer modes) — the behaviour is inferred, not decompiled.

nodes.label: Nuitka Native Packaging
nodes.rationale: Confirmed by 90+ NUITKA markers and the absence of base_library.zip/PYZ/_internal — so pyinstxtractor+pycdc does not apply, because there is no bytecode to decompile, only native machine code.

nodes.label: ZeeK Security Risk Findings
nodes.rationale: License and telemetry travel over plain HTTP to a fixed IP (MITM-exposed) and a Deriv API token is embedded in the binary, so the distribution model itself is the vulnerability.

nodes.label: ZeeK 3.0 Trading Robot
nodes.rationale: Python 3.13 + PySide6 binary-options robot for Deriv, compiled with Nuitka and shipped via Inno Setup — the reverse-engineering target that this project's BotTrader guards mirror.

nodes.label: Nuitka Constant-Blob Decompilation Limit
nodes.rationale: Nuitka serializes all constants into a compressed .rsrc blob unpacked only at runtime and accessed by index, so there is no static string-to-function linkage (xrefs = 0) and the exact martingale math is only observable by MITM of the live Deriv WSS.

nodes.label: Gale (Martingale) Algorithm
nodes.rationale: stake = baseStake x galeMultiplier^floor(losses/galeSplit); galeSplit exists so the level advances only every N losses, softening exposure growth compared with doubling on every single loss.

nodes.label: Soros (Profit Reinvestment) Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Only accumulated profit is reinvested and any loss zeroes it back to the base stake, so compounding risks winnings rather than principal — the inverse posture to Gale.

nodes.label: Pre-Start Config Validation
nodes.rationale: Sign conventions are enforced (stopLoss negative, stopWin positive, galeMultiplier >= 1) and a stop loss above 50% of balance only warns, since an aggressive but deliberate setting should not be blocked.

nodes.label: Fast Execution via Proposal Keeper

nodes.label: Live Tracking de Assertividade Virtual (virtStats)
nodes.rationale: Prevê o dígito alvo a cada tick e resolve no tick seguinte com vsignal para alimentar o medidor de assertividade em tempo real.

nodes.label: Next-Tick Settlement em Simulação
nodes.rationale: Garantir fidelidade estrita ao mercado aguardando a cotação do tick seguinte via deriv.tick antes de liquidar o contrato simulado.

nodes.label: Contrato Differ na Deriv
nodes.rationale: Aposta que o último dígito do tick seguinte não será a barreira selecionada (90% chance teórica, payout 9.5-10%, risco de cauda de 100% da stake).

nodes.label: Gestão de Martingale Normal e Parcial
nodes.norm_label: gestao de martingale normal e parcial
nodes.rationale: Martingale normal recupera a perda em 1 acerto exigindo banca maior; martingale parcial fraciona a recuperação reduzindo o drawdown.

nodes.label: Arquitetura das 8 Abas Analíticas
nodes.rationale: Separação das dimensões de trading: Operação, Lógicas, Vigilância, Laboratório, Validação, Risco, Esteira e Sistema.

nodes.label: Scanner de Vigilância Multivariado (5s)
nodes.rationale: Varredura periódica a cada 5s classificando ativos em Normal, Observação, Quebra de Regime ou Amostra Baixa para guiar a seleção de mercado.
